title: Greeting
prompt: Write a small Python program that asks for a person's name and favorite color, then prints a friendly greeting that includes both answers.
diagnosis_hooks: Separate the two inputs from the literal text the program should print.
Check whether the learner is storing user input as text or accidentally treating a name as a number.
Ask how the output should combine the stored values with the greeting words.

title: Even-or-odd
prompt: Ask the user for a whole number and report whether it is even or odd.
diagnosis_hooks: Distinguish a number's quotient from its remainder when dividing by two.
Check that the learner has converted the input into a whole number before testing it.
Use a small example to connect the remainder to the even-or-odd decision.

title: Countdown
prompt: Ask the user for a positive whole number and display a countdown from that number to zero, showing one number per line.
diagnosis_hooks: Clarify whether the starting value and zero are both included in the countdown.
Check the update direction and stopping condition together.
Watch for an off-by-one error caused by stopping before or after zero.

title: Average of a list
prompt: Given a non-empty list of numbers, calculate and display its average without using a built-in average helper.
diagnosis_hooks: Separate the running total from the number of items in the list.
Check that the divisor is the list length rather than the last valid index.
Ask what the exercise guarantees about an empty list before discussing the calculation.

title: Temperature converter
prompt: Define a function that converts a temperature from Celsius to Fahrenheit, then use the function to display the converted value for one input.
diagnosis_hooks: Keep the input temperature, converted value, and displayed result conceptually separate.
Check that the function receives the temperature and sends a value back to its caller.
Watch for a missing return that leaves the caller without the converted result.

title: Word counter
prompt: Given a sentence, count how many times each word appears and display the counts, treating uppercase and lowercase versions of a word as the same.
diagnosis_hooks: Normalize each word consistently before using it as a dictionary key.
Distinguish looking up an existing count from creating a new key.
Check whether splitting the sentence produces the intended word boundaries.
